2025-the-alabama-solution.title: The Alabama Solution
2025-the-alabama-solution.summary: The invite seems innocuous: Come cover the annual BBQ for incarcerated men at an Alabama state prison. But what filmmakers Andrew Jarecki ( Capturing the Friedmans , The Jinx ) and Charlotte Kaufman discover during that public relations event leads them down a serpentine investigative path. The pair unearth decades of horrific abuse; deplorable, inhumane conditions; shocking injustices; and numerous deaths within penitentiary walls where media cameras are not allowed. Through the use of contraband cellphones and interviews with men on the inside and relatives and others on the outside demanding elusive answers, this powerful documentary graphically details a system that is not only corrupt and ineffective but binds these men into a modern form of slavery. Edited seamlessly by Page Marsella, The Alabama Solution is a damning and disturbing indictment that looks at every facet of a broken institution, while also serving as a shout for accountability and justice. —Randy Myers

2025-the-buttercup-mafia.title: The Buttercup Mafia
2025-the-buttercup-mafia.summary: Play Trailer A trio of childish teens under the name “The Buttercup Mafia” find success in intimidating bullies in exchange for cash.

2025-the-hi-de-ho-show.title: The Hi De Ho Show
2025-the-hi-de-ho-show.summary: The ever-popular, only at MVFF Hi De Ho Show is back! Light years before tastemakers touted their tastes, eons before influencers infiltrated our imaginations, there was John Goddard, whose Village Music record store in Mill Valley was the go-to place for musicians (think Elvis C.), filmmakers (think George L.), and lovers of all things revolving at 45 rpm, 33⅓ rpm, and maybe even 78 rpm. Yet even Goddard missed some cool and iconic tracks on their first appearance—only to discover them years, sometimes decades, later. They’d show up on a movie or commercial soundtrack. Or maybe via his wife, Michael Blair, a dedicated follower of Queen. Veejaying clips from his personal archive, Goddard explores those ones-that-got-away—A-ha! moments and musical revelations that add up to a forever soundtrack. With gems from the’70s onwards, prepare to rock this town—and listen up for the likes of C. McVie, J. Hiatt, B. Raitt, B. Gees, and much, much more. —Z. Elton

2025-the-incredible-sensational-fiancee-.title: The Incredible, Sensational Fiancée of Sèyí Àjàyí
2025-the-incredible-sensational-fiancee-.summary: In Abbesi Akhemi’s stylish and comedic film, a renowned scholar’s public breakup sends her on a quest for revenge.

2025-the-long-labor.title: The Long Labor
2025-the-long-labor.summary: After losing her mother in childbirth, a Mexican immigrant grows up to become a certified midwife and nurse practitioner who joins forces with local women to offer dignified care and revive ancestral healing traditions for indigenous farmworker communities in Watsonville, CA.

2025-the-love-that-remains.title: The Love that Remains
2025-the-love-that-remains.summary: A disintegrating marriage takes center stage in this quirky, heartbreaking, and tenderly human tragicomedy. Icelandic director Hlynur Pálmason ( Godland ) creates an atmosphere that echoes an eavesdropping documentary, capturing each member of the family—dissatisfied artist mom Anna, emotionally isolated dad Magnus, world-weary teen daughter, rambunctious pair of young brothers, and marvelously charismatic dog—as they navigate a year of change in and around their remote home. The Icelandic landscape is stunning, the ocean unrelenting, and emotions kept carefully in check as the parents grapple with unequal post-separation desires and the kids seek outlets for their energy and frustration. Monty Python─esque humor, artful interspersed sequences, wild fantasy visions, and a dreamy piano score wrap around the narrative, keeping everything a bit off balance—just the way it might feel for anyone grappling with love, loss, an occasional vicious rooster, and one’s place in the unique world of their own family. —Deanna Quinones

2025-the-luminous-life.title: The Luminous Life
2025-the-luminous-life.summary: Play Trailer The Luminous Life is a wistful, romantic adventure through the winding streets of Lisbon, where 30-something Nicolau floats between past loves, uncertain futures, and the beautiful mess of in-between. After a breakup and still chasing a band that never quite made it, he moves through the city like a dreamer out of time—reconnecting with people, possibilities, and paths not taken. João Rosas crafts a tender, quietly radiant portrait of modern adulthood—full of humor, heart, and chance encounters that might just change everything. Lisbon pulses with life and memory, becoming both backdrop and companion in this gentle ode to hesitation, reinvention, and the soft courage of starting again. With its breezy rhythms and introspective charm, it echoes the spirit of French New Wave wanderers—intelligent, searching, and irresistibly human. —João Federici A Luminous Life ( Una Vida Luminos a) es una aventura romántica y nostálgica por las serpenteantes calles de Lisboa, donde Nicolau, de unos treinta años, flota entre amores pasados, futuros inciertos y el hermoso caos de lo intermedio. Tras una ruptura y aún persiguiendo a una banda que nunca llegó a despegar, se mueve por la ciudad como un soñador perdido en el tiempo, reconectando con personas, posibilidades y caminos no tomados. João Rosas crea un retrato tierno y silenciosamente radiante de la edad adulta moderna, lleno de humor, corazón y encuentros fortuitos que podrían cambiarlo todo. Lisboa late con vida y memoria, convirtiéndose tanto en escenario como en compañera en esta dulce oda a la duda, la reinvención y el delicado coraje de comenzar de nuevo. Con sus ritmos ligeros y encanto introspectivo, evoca el espíritu de los vagabundos de la Nouvelle Vague francesa: inteligentes, buscadores e irresistiblemente humanos. —João Federici

2025-the-mastermind.title: The Mastermind
2025-the-mastermind.summary: Josh O’Connor ( Mothering Sunday , MVFF44) charms as bumbling scammer JB Mooney. You can’t help but root for the out-of-work architect when he has an epiphany at an art museum—why doesn’t he just steal some paintings and sell them? It’s a bit audacious but he is sure that with the right help, he can pull it off. He does, but nothing goes according to plan. An accomplice drops out, the new one can’t keep his mouth shut, the FBI is onto him, the Mob has caught wind of his scheme, and worst of all, his wife is mad at him. Bolstered by a jazzy score and a cast of recognizable faces, Kelly Reichardt’s ( Certain Women , MVFF39) deconstruction of the heist film will have you constantly wondering who JB lies to more: the people in his life or himself. —Bri’anna Moore

2025-the-mysterious-gaze-of-the-flamingo.title: The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo
2025-the-mysterious-gaze-of-the-flamingo.summary: A Western and desert fable unlike any other, The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo takes us to a small, isolated mining town in 1982 Chile, where a mysterious illness is said to spread through the looks exchanged between lovers at the town’s defiantly queer cabaret bar. As fear and superstition take hold, Lidia—a curious pre-teen growing up among trans women and the bar’s beloved regulars—sets out in search of the truth. Winner of the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at Cannes, Diego Céspedes’s luminous debut blends melodrama, magical realism, and coming-of-age tenderness with striking humor, heartfelt performances, and the stunning beauty of the desert landscape. Through silence, gesture, and deep affection, it captures both the fragility and fierce strength of chosen family under threat. Flamingo is bold, deeply moving, and wildly original—a tribute to love, memory, and the courage to face the future with resilience and without fear. —João Federici Un western y una fábula del desierto como ninguna otra, La mirada misteriosa del flamenco nos lleva a un pequeño y aislado pueblo minero del norte de Chile en 1982, donde se dice que una enfermedad misteriosa se transmite a través de las miradas que se cruzan entre amantes en el cabaret del pueblo —un espacio abiertamente queer que desafía las normas. A medida que el miedo y la superstición se apoderan de la comunidad, Lidia —una niña preadolescente curiosa que crece entre mujeres trans y los entrañables asiduos del bar— emprende la búsqueda de la verdad. Ganadora del Premio del Jurado Un Certain Regard en Cannes, la luminosa ópera prima de Diego Céspedes combina melodrama, realismo mágico y ternura del despertar adolescente con un humor sorprendente, actuaciones conmovedoras y la belleza deslumbrante del paisaje desértico. A través del silencio, los gestos y un profundo afecto, retrata tanto la fragilidad como la fuerza feroz de una familia elegida bajo amenaza. Flamenco es audaz, profundamente emotiva y totalmente original: un homenaje al amor, la memoria y el coraje para enfrentar el futuro con resiliencia y sin miedo. —João Federici

2025-the-perfect-neighbor.title: The Perfect Neighbor
2025-the-perfect-neighbor.summary: In the wide-open spaces between the low-rise rental homes in a Marion County, Florida, neighborhood, a fleet of kids routinely play, whoop, and holler. A middle-aged single woman routinely objects to their “trespassing” and periodically calls 911. Is it reasonable to be annoyed by loud children? Is it relevant that she is white and the kids are Black? One night, claiming to fear for her life, she fires a gun through her closed and locked front door, striking the mother of some of the children. Did she feel justified by Florida’s Stand Your Ground law? Geeta Gandbhir explores these questions in this remarkable documentary. The director confines her film to police recordings—body-camera footage and in-custody investigative interviews—that provide privileged access and professional distance, while inviting us to make our own judgments and recognize our personal assumptions and biases. Gandbhir received the Sundance Film Festival US Documentary Directing Award for her unique saga of a true-crime tragedy. —Michael Fox

2025-the-plague.title: The Plague
2025-the-plague.summary: A Lord of the Flies -like atmosphere settles over a boys’ water polo camp in writer-director Charlie Polinger’s arresting first feature, in which a kid’s mysterious skin affliction gives his teammates license to bully. That’s the situation that greets Ben (Everett Blunck, Griffin in Summer , MVFF47) as he joins the camp. The insecure tween is desperate to win the approval of the cool clique but more than water polo, the true sport these young athletes enjoy is picking on Eli (Kenny Rasmussen), a misfit with a vibrant rash his teammates claim is contagious. Ben can join in the abuse or defend Eli—at the risk of becoming the bullies’ next target. The young cast is simply extraordinary, joined by Joel Edgerton as the camp’s checked-out coach, in a drama that builds its unease from our childhood fears of not fitting in, throwing us into the deep end alongside Ben. —Tim Grierson

2025-the-president-s-cake.title: The President's Cake
2025-the-president-s-cake.summary: Iraqi President Saddam Hussein liked to celebrate his birthday, even demanding that school children nationwide bake him cakes—despite daunting food shortages in the waning years of his regime. Nine-year-old Lamia, who lives with her grandmother in a remote marshland, has the dubious luck to be “picked” as the student to produce the cake for the Supreme Leader’s fete. This near-impossible task forces them (plus Lamia’s pet rooster Hindi) to travel to the city for scarce basic ingredients. There, Lamia ditches Granny and joins her best friend Saeed in search of the elusive supplies, the day evolving into a sometimes-fraught adventure. Writer-director Hasan Hadi uses his own youth as the springboard for his first feature, a remarkable story of friendship, discovery, and understanding, as well as perseverance and loss, as seen through a child’s eyes. The first Iraqi feature to play at Cannes, this big-hearted drama won the festival’s Camera D’Or. —Dennis Harvey

2025-the-ramba-effect.title: The Ramba Effect
2025-the-ramba-effect.summary: Play Trailer A majestic Asian elephant takes her first steps toward freedom in this immersive, purpose-driven documentary. Meet Ramba, who endured 50 years of isolation in a Chilean circus, as she embarks on an extraordinary 2,550-mile journey to her new home at Elephant Sanctuary Brazil, guided by compassionate experts and a devoted team of volunteers. The film puts us front and center in the rescue effort, giving us a rare chance to become acquainted with the liberated pachyderm and witness the incredible dedication of the people who are fighting to give her a fresh start. The bigger picture is the critical need to end animal captivity in zoos and circuses. But the intimate story will grab your heart as you witness Ramba’s fraught and brave journey, then rejoice at the sight of this sensitive, emotional being—relaxed, befriended, and finally free, in the joyful last part of her life. —Deanna Quinones Una majestuosa elefanta asiática da sus primeros pasos hacia la libertad en este documental inmersivo y lleno de propósito. Conozcan a Ramba, quien soportó 50 años de aislamiento en un circo chileno, mientras emprende un extraordinario viaje de 4,100 kilómetros hacia su nuevo hogar en Elephant Sanctuary Brasil, acompañada por expertos compasivos y un dedicado equipo de voluntarios. La película nos sitúa en primera fila del rescate, ofreciéndonos la rara oportunidad de conocer a este paquidermo liberado y de presenciar la increíble dedicación de quienes luchan por darle un nuevo comienzo. En última instancia, la cuestión central es la urgente necesidad de poner fin a la cautividad de los animales en zoológicos y circos. Pero esta íntima historia atrapará tu corazón mientras sigues el arriesgado y valiente viaje de Ramba, y luego te llenará de alegría al verla relajada, acompañada de cariño y finalmente libre, disfrutando de la última etapa de su vida. —Deanna Quinones

2025-the-scene.title: The Scene
2025-the-scene.summary: Play Trailer Azadeh is a young girl who loves acting, and in order to get a small role in a movie, she forces herself to do things that jeopardize her daily routine and family tradition.

2025-the-scout.title: The Scout
2025-the-scout.summary: Working in film production sounds glamorous but often isn’t, a truth Paula González-Nasser explores in her absorbing directorial debut. This incisive, grounded feature follows Sofia (Mimi Davila), an exhausted and underappreciated location scout working in New York City. Inundated by voicemails, parking tickets, and demands from producers, Sofia struggles to find artistic validation in the monotony of her below-the-line role. Although The Scout is tinged with an everyday sort of melancholy, it’s also a striking character study. Each location Sofia visits throughout the day is a vignette that opens a window into the life of the film’s protagonist as well as those of the people she meets. Rooted in González-Nasser’s own experiences working on shows like Difficult People and Mrs. Fletcher , The Scout boasts gorgeous cinematography and an impressively lived-in feel that makes this nuanced, observational debut a perfect ode to filmmaking—both the lonely and beautiful parts. —Kate Bove

2025-the-sun-and-the-wind.title: The Sun and the Wind
2025-the-sun-and-the-wind.shorts_program: Shorts: Animation Nation, a Family Film College Showcase
2025-the-sun-and-the-wind.summary: Two cosmic rivals battle it out, only to realize that even the fiercest power can’t beat a small spark of warmth. Based on a classic Aesop’s fable.

2025-tripawds.title: Tripawds
2025-tripawds.summary: Play Trailer With their delightful Tripawds , Bay Area filmmakers Jay Rosenblatt and Stephanie Rapp capture the annual San Francisco gathering of three-legged dogs and their humans, a celebration of these resilient canines and their dedicated owners.

2025-underland.title: Underland
2025-underland.summary: For centuries, what lies below—and out of sight—has fascinated humans. Many of our oldest and most beloved stories are about descents into unseeable underworlds. In Underland , an adaptation of Robert Macfarlane’s bestselling book of the same name, director Robert Petit examines why subterranean spaces hold such a timeless allure. Split into chapters, the documentary spotlights an archaeologist’s attempts to map a sacred Mayan cave; an urban explorer’s efforts to preserve present-day tunnel-dwellers’ stories; and a scientist’s search for dark matter in a sterile lab hidden kilometers below Earth’s surface. Narrated by two-time Oscar nominee Sandra Hüller ( Anatomy of a Fall , MVFF46) and produced by Golden Lion-winning filmmaker Darren Aronofsky ( The Whale , MVFF45), this beautifully lensed, brilliantly scored, and grippingly philosophical documentary suggests that the key to humanity’s future exists in the many layers of history preserved in the darkness of abandoned subway systems and in the hallowed bellies of caves. —Kate Bove

2025-wake-up-dead-man-a-knives-out-myste.title: Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery
2025-wake-up-dead-man-a-knives-out-myste.summary: Play Trailer Daniel Craig reprises his role as Benoit Blanc in this third chapter in Rian Johnson’s Knives Out series of murder mysteries, as the brilliant (and charming) private eye seeks to uncover whodunit this time.

2025-wanna-die-wanna-kill.title: Wanna Die Wanna Kill
2025-wanna-die-wanna-kill.shorts_program: Shorts: The Dark End of the Street
2025-wanna-die-wanna-kill.summary: A melancholic teen finds a fellow adolescent who she thinks is a kindred spirit.

2025-white-crow.title: White Crow
2025-white-crow.summary: Play Trailer A young woman in Stalin's Russia faces a life-or-death choice after carrying out a daring act of protest.

2025-won-t-be-around.title: Won't be Around
2025-won-t-be-around.summary: Director Terry Blade offers an anthem to inner strength in this music video.

2025-work-from-home.title: Work from Home
2025-work-from-home.summary: A young woman's office job turns surreal when she is forced into COVID isolation.

2025-yanuni.title: Yanuni
2025-yanuni.summary: Produced by Leonardo Di Caprio, this tense, captivating documentary dives deep into the dangerous politics of the Amazon rainforest. Indigenous chief and climate justice leader Juma Xipaia has survived six assassination attempts. Now, she and her husband, Brazilian environmental protection agency official Hugo Loss, are expecting a child. Together this power couple devote their lives to defending the people and rainforests of their homeland, while raising a family. Their opposition is powerful—and dangerous: cash-fueled government drilling crews, operating out of illegal mining camps as they search for gold and other riches deep underground. Filmmaker Richard Ladkani masterfully weaves a complicated story crafting breathtaking shots of stunning landscapes with intense handheld footage of the life-and-death struggles facing a small, mighty resistance. Combining electrifying jungle action with intense personal drama, the film follows this passionate, committed couple as they battle gold miners and big business to create a healthy, hopeful future for their children, and for all of us. —Brendan Peterson Producido por Leonardo DiCaprio, este documental tenso y cautivador se adentra en la peligrosa política de la selva amazónica. La jefa indígena y líder de justicia climática Juma Xipaia ha sobrevivido seis intentos de asesinato. Ahora, ella y su esposo, el funcionario de la agencia brasileña de protección ambiental Hugo Loss, esperan un hijo. Juntos, esta poderosa pareja dedica su vida a defender a la gente y los bosques de su tierra natal, mientras crían a su familia. Su oposición es fuerte y peligrosa: equipos de perforación gubernamentales movidos por dinero, operando desde campamentos mineros ilegales en busca de oro y otras riquezas bajo tierra. El cineasta Richard Ladkani teje magistralmente una historia compleja, combinando impresionantes tomas de paisajes espectaculares con intensas imágenes con cámara en mano de las luchas a vida o muerte que enfrenta esta pequeña pero poderosa resistencia. Al combinar la acción electrizante de la selva con un drama personal profundo, la película sigue a esta apasionada y comprometida pareja mientras lucha contra mineros de oro y grandes corporaciones para crear un futuro saludable y esperanzador para sus hijos… y para todos nosotros. —Brendan Peterson

2025-your-night-is-my-day.title: Your Night is My Day
2025-your-night-is-my-day.summary: Worlds apart, two 20-somethings collide over a tenuous connection, dependent on computer screens and time zones to reveal their true selves

2026-2392-miles.title: 2392 Miles
2026-2392-miles.summary: Flowing water and memories, the mind's journey to find home in the unfamiliar.

2026-a-bay-to-live-on.title: A Bay to Live On
2026-a-bay-to-live-on.summary: Across the San Francisco Bay, subsistence fishers below the poverty line depend on their catch to feed their families, even as decades of pollution poison the waters.

2026-wu-ming-nu-hai.title: Wu Ming Nü Hai
2026-wu-ming-nu-hai.summary: Play Trailer Born in the wake of China’s controversial one-child policy, six-year-old Wang Juan (Cao Ruofan) finds her life completely upended by her mother’s pregnancy. The young girl is soon taken from her rural home—where kite-flying and swimming fill her days—and brought to the home of a discordant, childless couple. Abandoned in an unfamiliar city with her new legal guardians, Juan strives to find a sense of belonging, a struggle that only worsens when she’s uprooted twice more before turning 18 years old. Anchored by a powerful performance from Resurrection’s Li Gengxi, who plays teenage Juan, Zou Jing’s confident debut is an achingly tender coming-of-age drama. And while it never shies away from the harrowing realities of the political directive that dehumanized and haunted so many, A Girl Unknown also reaffirms the undeniable, striking hopefulness of a young person’s belief in love and self. —Kate Bove

2026-a-long-winter.title: A Long Winter
2026-a-long-winter.summary: With an intimate tale of tender heartbreak, 45 Years (MVFF38) and All of Us Strangers filmmaker Andrew Haigh transports his observant temperament and distinctive lens into the unsteadiness of domestic life to the Mountain West of the early 1950s. Based on a short story by Colm Tóibín, a perfect literary match for Haigh’s melancholic rhythms, A Long Winter follows young Mike (Fred Hechinger, with his finest turn in a rapidly bourgeoning career) and his resolute father (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) in the overwhelming aftermath of Mike’s brother leaving for the Korean War, and his mother (Caitríona Balfe) disappearing in a snow storm. While the icy temperatures settle in across an increasingly fruitless search, something slowly begins to thaw within Mike as he becomes aware of his own passions and sexual longings. Juxtaposed against the relentless majesty of snow-clad heights, Haigh’s painterly interiors and soulful depths gorgeously articulate repressed, unspoken emotions that refuse to continue hibernating. —Tomris Laffly

2026-a-new-inferno.title: A New Inferno
2026-a-new-inferno.summary: In Nita Blum and Jonathan Pickett’s A New Inferno , paramedics race to save the lives of heatstroke victims using a radical new treatment.

2026-a-new-normal.title: A New Normal
2026-a-new-normal.summary: A New Normal is a short film created using Augmented Reality, that subverts the limitations of digital intimacy to create a story about warmth, hope, and family.

2026-a-prayer-for-the-dying.title: A Prayer for the Dying
2026-a-prayer-for-the-dying.summary: Play Trailer Dara Van Dusen’s feature debut is a visually compelling Western set in 1870 in Friendship, Wisconsin. In the settlement—a place with not much more than a general store, a church, and a handful of smallholdings—everyone ekes out the barest of existences, including Jacob (Johnny Flynn), the town’s sheriff, preacher, and undertaker. When an outbreak of diphtheria threatens the community’s stability, he and the village doctor (John C. Reilly) navigate the threat as best they know how: initially, by concealing it, hoping it will subside. But Jacob finds himself torn between his roles as a leader, a husband and father, and a Civil War veteran navigating the haunting memories of his service, as another threat, a wildfire, looms on the horizon. With striking cinematography and sound design, Van Dusen creates a world both familiar and eerily apocalyptic, driven by great central performances. It’s a notable achievement for a first-time filmmaker. —Zoë Elton

2026-a-talent-for-murder.title: A Talent for Murder
2026-a-talent-for-murder.summary: Play Trailer In Anton Corbijn’s playful thriller, Oscar winner Helen Mirren delivers a fiendishly juicy portrayal of the legendary mystery author Patricia Highsmith in an imaginary scenario with a wicked sense of humor. Based on Joanna Murray-Smith’s play, Switzerland (adapted for the screen by the playwright herself), the story follows the famously tough Highsmith while the retired author receives a visit from over-ambitious publishing rep Edward Ridgeway (Alden Ehrenreich, unpredictable at every turn) at her handsome Swiss Alps home. The year is 1995 and the talented Mr. Ridgeway has but one mission: convince Highsmith to conjure up a final Tom Ripley murder mystery, poised to be a bestseller. As the equally stubborn and deliberate Ridgeway and Highsmith face off across a mazy creative process where their unknowable instincts often clash, the line between reality and fiction blurs in unimaginable ways, spilling both the blood and the beans as stylishly as a Highsmith novel. —Tomris Laffly

2026-a-town-called-needville.title: A Town Called Needville
2026-a-town-called-needville.summary: Composed of black-and-white 35mm photographs, A Town Called Needville traces filmmaker Audrey Lane's inpatient stay at an all-women’s mental health facility in Texas.

2026-all-american-girls.title: All American Girls
2026-all-american-girls.summary: If you’ve ever pined for an American Girl doll or its tiny, perfect accessories, this documentary is right in your dollhouse. Director Christy Wegener ( I Am Vanessa Guillen ) pulls back the meticulously crafted curtain on the venture that quietly began as Pleasant Company and vaulted into the multimillion-dollar empire known as American Girl®. Featuring an exclusive interview with founder Pleasant Rowland, along with archival footage and insights from original staffers and diehard fans, this energetic deep dive examines the feminist and academic framework behind the characters and the triumphs and controversies that shaped the booming business. Get the backstory on how Rowland dreamed up the historical dolls and their intricate worlds. Meet the adults who keep aflame the passion that defined their childhoods in the ‘80s, ‘90s, and early 2000s. And revel in feisty memes and multimedia artwork that illuminate the brand’s unparalleled influence and ongoing cultural relevance. —D. Quinones

2026-are-we-still-married.title: Are We Still Married?
2026-are-we-still-married.summary: Director Kit Steinkellner devises a surprise development for a young couple which forces them to wonder Are We Still Married?

2026-at-the-stage-when.title: At the Stage When
2026-at-the-stage-when.summary: Intimate and observational, At the Stage When follows a young urban couple experiencing societal pressure around parenthood.

2026-avedon.title: Avedon
2026-avedon.summary: Academy Award®-winning director Ron Howard traces the man behind the camera and the iconic images that made Richard Avedon one of the most influential photographers of the 20th century. From the stark white backgrounds that became his signature to his unforgettable portraits of cultural icons like Charlie Chaplin and Marilyn Monroe, Avedon redefined the visual language of fashion and celebrity. Yet beyond the glamour, the film delves into a childhood home built on staged happiness, revealing how those early experiences informed his personal life and artistic vision. With unprecedented access to personal archives, home movies, never-before-seen photographs, and interviews with his son John Avedon, fashion titan Calvin Klein, art dealer Larry Gagosian, and famous muses Isabella Rossellini, Twiggy, and Lauren Hutton, Avedon offers a rare glimpse into the deeply private artist whose extraordinary body of work continues to shape the worlds of photography, fashion, and culture. —Michelle Svenson Justin Wilkes in Conversation Tuesday, October 6, 4:30 PM | SEQ 1

2026-bedford-park.title: Bedford Park
2026-bedford-park.summary: A car becomes the connective tissue of director Stephanie Ahn’s absorbing debut, gradually drawing two broken souls together and giving them the space to see one another. Korean American Audrey (Moon Choi) is in her 30s and obsessed with having a child. After her mother is in an auto accident, Audrey confronts Eli (Son Suk-ku), the man responsible for the crash. Ahn deftly steers the upheaval of their encounter into an increasingly intimate, if fumbling, relationship. The air between the characters is thick. The Korean concept of han waltzes across the screen with allure to spare: True sorrow outlives rage, taking the shape of endurance. With tranquil assurance, the director transforms the film’s structure and interiors into an expressive world entirely her own; simmering emotional wells that sit within each character are potent and extreme. The winner of the 2026 Sundance US Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature holds you tight and doesn't let go. —Ivonne Cotorruelo

2026-being-dead-should-be-easy.title: Being Dead Should Be Easy
2026-being-dead-should-be-easy.summary: In Claire Harris Matson and Drew Brandon Jones’s very funny Being Dead Should Be Easy , a shiva is the perfect place to discuss planning one’s own mortal passing.

2026-amarga-navidad.title: Amarga Navidad
2026-amarga-navidad.summary: Play Trailer Who owns a story when an artist turns someone else's life into fiction? And what happens when that person recognizes themselves in the work? Pedro Almodóvar ( The Room Next Door , MVFF47) returns with a playful, layered story about friendship, loss, and the slippery boundary between life and fiction. In parallel stories, Elsa, a filmmaker grieving her mother and struggling with debilitating migraines, retreats to Lanzarote, while Raúl, a celebrated filmmaker, transforms the life of his longtime collaborator Mónica into a screenplay. As fiction and reality begin to overlap, Almodóvar turns his camera toward the very act of creating, exploring memory, artistic ownership, and the complicated line between inspiration and appropriation. The director’s unmistakable visual flair is everywhere, with colors shifting between worlds and singer-songwriter Chavela Vargas's haunting music adding an emotional pulse. Full of wit, melodrama, beautiful performances, and Almodóvar's singular sensibility, Bitter Christmas is the latest invitation into the cinematic universe of one of our most beloved filmmakers. — João Federici

2026-boss-cat.title: Boss Cat
2026-boss-cat.summary: Play Trailer Twenty-something Sonja (Olivia Hargroder, superb in her feature film debut) is an ambitious, sassy, raging bundle of creative energy whose dreams of artistic self-expression are only matched by her desire for independence. Born with Trisomy 21 (Down Syndrome), she refuses to allow biology to be her destiny and defies all obstacles—and people—that block her way. But when her mom dies, Grandma Doris has other plans for Sonja—in a board-and-care facility. Sonja's anger and grief find an empowering outlet when her friend Hakim, a Sudanese refugee, introduces her to krump street dancing. First-time director Genevieve Clay-Smith collaborated with a fully inclusive cast and crew on this funny, fiery, and family-friendly film that provides a uniquely compelling and beautiful testament to the power of resilience, independence, and love. Produced by Bus Stop Films, a company dedicated to end-to-end inclusivity in film production. —K.D. Davis Appropriate for grades 7-12 (ages 12-17)

2026-brave-cat.title: Brave Cat
2026-brave-cat.summary: Play Trailer Kona is a young cat who dwells in the forest with her loving mother and her wise grandma . All forest creatures live together in harmony except for the solitary human who scouts the countryside with his ill-tempered hunting dogs, capturing animals for a traveling circus. When he snares her mom, Kona embarks on a quest that takes her through the forest, over snowy mountains, and down to the ocean’s shore on a quest to find her parent. While she begins her journey alone, she soon finds help and companionship from Colin, an adorable—if pesty—pup, and brave Bernard, a runaway circus bear. Oscar®-winning Chilean animator Gabriel Osorio’s beautifully imaginative settings (inspired by the Patagonian landscape) and intricate handmade production design weave a family-friendly tale of bravery, determination, and forgiveness. Winner of the 2026 Annecy International Animation Film Festival Annecy Presents Audience Award. —KD Davis

2026-brian.title: Brian
2026-brian.summary: “Today is going to be a good day,” repeats Brian (rising star Ben Wang, superb) to his reflection in the mirror each morning before the usual day of disappointments and misunderstandings begins. Prone to frequent outbursts due to his mental health issues, the optimistic high-schooler and his good intentions often derail into comical calamity amidst run-ins with his brother, classmates, teachers, and therapist, who are all too familiar with his emotional flare-ups. When he accidentally self-sabotages his dreams of performing in the school play, Brian finds a new calling: running for senior class president. Armed with a sharply realized script from Late Night scribe Mike Scollins that deftly balances uproarious jokes with earned heartfelt insight, and a murderer’s row of crackling performances from some of comedy’s finest talents, director Will Ropp’s breakout hit of SXSW delivers one of the most memorable coming-of-age films in years. —Landon Zakheim

2026-bunker.title: Bunker
2026-bunker.summary: Play Trailer Even the most beautiful love stories can start with a misunderstanding. In Florian Zeller’s ( The Father , MVFF43) elegant psychological drama, Javier Bardem and Penelope Cruz are successful professionals (architect and editor, respectively) married to their work, and to each other. Their “misunderstanding” is a story Miguel (Bardem) recounts: On their first date his allergies, mistaken by Sofia (Cruz) for tears of empathy, led to their first kiss. Misunderstandings deepen when Miguel meets a tech billionaire (Paul Dano, chillingly familiar) who wants him to design a luxury bunker in Hawai’i—a project antithetical to the ideals the couple once shared. Tensions at home escalate when the blue-collar neighbor punctures a hole in the couple’s garden wall to build a window for his own garage. With an exquisite soundtrack by Volker Bertelmann ( Conclave , MVFF47), Bunker asks us to consider the silos and walls we build, and the fears we have of knocking them down. – K.D. Davis

2026-burgundy.title: Burgundy
2026-burgundy.summary: Michael Dweck and Gregory Kershaw are modern-day masters of creative nonfiction with their melancholic portrayals of one-of-a-kind traditions and the communities who proudly carry them. After focusing on truffle-sniffing canines and humans ( The Truffle Hunters , MVFF43), and Argentine cowboys and cowgirls ( Gaucho Gaucho , 2024), the duo turns their dreamy lens to the irresistible flavors of the Burgundy region and its colorful personalities of different socioeconomic realities. From a dapper vineyard worker with an Alain Delon flair, to a service old hand so committed to the delicious ingredients of his menu that you might just applaud his disarming theatrics, individuals that construct Burgundy’s many layers all aim to make a lasting impression like that last great bottle of wine you’ve slurped and can’t forget. A romantic cinematic journey that often winks at the pleasures and techniques of the French New Wave, Burgundy is here to caress your palate with its silky aromas and sophisticated aftertaste. —Tomris Laffly

2026-card-trick.title: Card Trick
2026-card-trick.summary: Two friends, Simon and Teddy, discover the marvels and mishaps of a little magic that tests their friendship.

2026-careless.title: Careless
2026-careless.summary: A breakup from the point of view of a young woman hoping to glue the pieces together but discovering that some broken things cannot be fixed.

2026-carl-sagan-we-are-made-of-star-stuf.title: Carl Sagan: We are Made of Star Stuff
2026-carl-sagan-we-are-made-of-star-stuf.summary: For many, cosmologist Carl Sagan was the face of space exploration, scientific inquiry, and insatiable curiosity, his enthusiasm contagious. Nanette Burstein’s fascinating documentary reveals the man behind the legend. Sagan’s involvement in the Voyager satellite program that was instrumental not only in discovering details about Earth’s neighboring planets but also paved the way for serious discussion about extraterrestrial life catapulted the university professor and NASA advisor into the stratosphere. But with additional fame as an iconoclast (author of Cosmos , activist against nuclear proliferation) came a heavy toll: a fractured family life and difficulty adapting to his role in it, until he met his soulmate, Anne. In this absorbing evocation of Sagan’s life, Burstein employs home movies, audio archives, candid testimonials, and extraordinary space photography to tell the story of a true globalist who loved being an ambassador for the human condition, the spread of knowledge, and our relationship with the universe. —Sterling Hedgpeth

2026-cat-and-mouse.title: Cat and Mouse
2026-cat-and-mouse.summary: A jazzy, sassy musical tale of Mouse Detective Quill on the trail of his longtime nemesis and secret crush, Cat Burglar Juliette.

2026-chasing-dragonflies.title: Chasing Dragonflies
2026-chasing-dragonflies.summary: After 40 years running his grocery store, 72-year-old Chuck reflects on his South Korean childhood and his lifelong devotion to Philadelphia's Caribbean community.

2026-chirp-talker.title: Chirp Talker
2026-chirp-talker.summary: Delighted by the birds chattering on her balcony, Audrey invents a bird-language translator to unlock their secret, playful conversations.

2026-cicada.title: Cicada
2026-cicada.summary: For 17 years, Cicada has worked faithfully and flawlessly in a gray office, yet remains ignored and bullied, his entire life bound to a strict schedule.

2026-closure.title: Closure
2026-closure.summary: Play Trailer Poland's Vistula River rushes along—an evocative image transformed into a visually haunting depiction of grief, encapsulating the indescribable hollowness that loss leaves behind within the living. Krzysztof was just 16 when he disappeared, last spotted by a CCTV camera as he stood on a bridge spanning the river. His father, Daniel, compulsively combs the water, refusing to give up. Following Daniel's dogged search for any trace of his missing son, the waterway becomes a space where hope and extreme grief collide. What elevates Closure is Michael Marczak's remarkable directorial precision and striking visual work, giving this nonfiction the dramatic force of a narrative film. A standout at Sundance and winner of Thessaloniki Documentary Film Festival's highest honor, the Golden Alexander, it dives deep into the shadows of the human soul with its devastating exploration of loss, becoming the cinematic equivalent of a river that flows endlessly. — Ivonne Cotorruelo

2026-constellations-of-the-sea.title: Constellations of the Sea
2026-constellations-of-the-sea.summary: A 17-year-old filmmaker joins a Maldives research team documenting the fight to protect endangered whale sharks amid a global tourism industry.

2026-coward.title: Coward
2026-coward.summary: Play Trailer In his previous films Girl (2018) and Close (2022), celebrated Belgian filmmaker Lukas Dhont explored the delicate emotional bonds between vulnerable characters. His third feature ups the stakes, bringing those concerns to the battlefield, as he focuses on two young soldiers who fall in love amidst the carnage of war. Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne shared the Best Actor prize at the Cannes Film Festival for their unguarded portrayals of, respectively, Pierre, a shy young farmer struggling to find his voice and overcome his fear, and the proudly theatrical Francis, who spearheads a series of performances to entertain his fellow troops. This tender World War I drama subverts preconceived notions about masculinity and warfare, and Macchia (making his big-screen debut) is especially affecting as a young man who discovers an unexpected romance. Set against the brutality of combat, C oward draws inspiration from actual cross-dressing theater revues that took place during the Great War, examining how sexual identity, intimacy, and survival were interwoven during that bloody conflict. —Tim Grierson

2026-crocodile.title: Crocodile
2026-crocodile.summary: Hibiscus tea standing in for blood, shots of bodies vanishing from the landscape, cars that fly. The set is a small village in Kaduna, Nigeria. A group of teenagers brimming with cinephile passion plunges into a sea of adventure, creating small films that swap out their present for a future world. The village’s lack of electricity conspires against the creation of their work but doesn’t give the group dramatic pause as their films start gaining international traction and support. More than a decade since it began, the collective known as The Critics is still making films. In Crocodile , director Pietra Brettkelly alongside the Critics themselves, weaves the cinematic alchemy of a coming-of-age story with the pulse of a band of young dreamers who thread naked police brutality and a broken system into handstitched sci-fi magic. —Ivonne Cotorruelo

2026-elephants-in-the-fog.title: Elephants in the Fog
2026-elephants-in-the-fog.summary: Play Trailer In a village in southern Nepal, Pirati is the matriarch of a Kinnar community, a third-gender tradition recognized in that country, where families form through chosen bonds of care rather than blood. When Apsara, one of Pirati’s daughters, disappears during a nightly patrol as the villagers keep watch for wild elephants, Pirati begins her own search. As the mystery opens wounds within the community, she wrestles with a difficult choice: remain with the family that gave her a home or pursue a new life with the man she loves. Around them, wild elephants move through the darkness, revered and feared, a haunting presence that echoes the film’s questions about belonging and otherness. Abinash Bikram Shah’s remarkable first feature is both a tense, immersive thriller and a tender portrait of chosen family, finding beauty in ritual, humor, desire, and everyday life. Noé Bach’s stunning cinematography makes the forest feel almost alive, while Frederic Alvarez’s haunting score draws us deeper into Pirati’s journey. Winner of the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at Cannes, Elephants in the Fog announces a filmmaker with a remarkably assured vision. —João Federici

guests.role: Actor | Recipient of the MVFF Acting Award

2026-enjoy-your-visit.title: Enjoy Your Visit
2026-enjoy-your-visit.summary: In Enjoy Your Visit , an African American actress cosplays as a slave at a tourist-based historical site.

2026-everest-the-other-side.title: Everest: The Other Side
2026-everest-the-other-side.summary: Play Trailer Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson became extreme sports stars in 2018 when they were the first to ski down Lhotse, the Everest-adjacent, fourth tallest mountain in the world. For their next challenge, the couple intended to scale Everest’s rarely attempted north face and then ski down from the summit. After a tragedy, Morrison presses on alone. His tenacity and spiritual intensity in overcoming grief, not to mention the awesome physical obstacles posed by Everest makes him one of those rare true-life adventurers whose exploits go farther than fiction. Everest: The Other Side captures Morrison’s extraordinary and risky 2025 ascent in images made all the more compelling because co-director Jimmy Chin is climbing next to Morrison, facing many of the same perils. Chin’s cinematography—along with that of Clair Popkin and Christopher Murray—and Morrison’s epic determination add up to a thrilling documentary. —Larry Gross

2026-everybody-to-kenmure-street.title: Everybody to Kenmure Street
2026-everybody-to-kenmure-street.summary: Play Trailer On the morning of Eid al-Fitr, as Muslims prepare to celebrate the end of Ramadan, tenants in a small Glasgow district notice an Immigration Enforcement van outside their windows. When two longtime neighbors are detained, text alerts set off a chain of events that quickly transforms the street into the site of an extraordinary act of solidarity. Blending crowdsourced mobile phone footage, archival material, interviews, and creative dramatizations featuring performances by Emma Thompson and Kate Dickie, the documentary captures the real-life standoff between residents and authorities. Taking on a nonconformist structure, the film conveys both the urgency of the moment and the deeper histories of migration, racism, and activism that shaped the city. At once deeply local and universally resonant, it is a testament to what can happen when a community refuses to look away. Winner of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival Special Jury Award for Civil Resistance. —Michelle Svenson

2026-everytime.title: Everytime
2026-everytime.summary: Play Trailer Austrian writer/director Sandra Wollner‘s Cannes Un Certain Regard Award winner begins with a calmly observed domestic situation. Divorced mom Ella (Minichmayr) gets ready to go on vacation while managing her squabbling daughters, teenage Jessica (Carla Hutterman) and precocious Melli (Lotte Schirin Keiling), with Jessica preferring to get high in the company of her cute boyfriend Lux (Tristán López). Before they can leave, tragedy devastates the family. A year later, the survivors take the interrupted journey to the sun-drenched Spanish resort Tenerife, and the drama becomes a unique, immersive exploration of what it means to experience grief. Woolner and her gifted cinematographer Christopher Oke (who shot 2024’s similarly themed and widely acclaimed Aftersun ) penetrate the unassuming surface of things to create a disquieting, disorienting atmosphere of dreamlike, almost Lynchian uncertainty, anchored by Minichmayr and Keiling's brilliant performances. Everytime asks us, in superbly subtle fashion, to reimagine the ways in which it is and is not possible to live through loss and resume living an everyday life. —Larry Gross

2026-extra-geography.title: Extra Geography
2026-extra-geography.summary: Play Trailer Idiosyncratic besties Flic and Minna are a pair of committed overachievers at their stately British boarding school for girls, spending their days playing lacrosse and aspiring to a pitch-perfect Oxbridge-bound future. But surely, thriving at a top university would demand one to be more “worldly”—as in, seasoned in romance. Once our novice wooers decide to practice falling in love with the next random person they see (who’s no other than their fretful geography teacher, Miss Delavigne), Molly Manners’ infinitely witty debut unfolds cheekily around the high-stakes canvas of adolescence with great empathy and a droll sense of humor. Extraordinary newcomers Marni Duggan and Galaxie Clear are instant stars in this winsome coming-of-age tale for the ages, as proudly British as high tea, Shakespeare, and Jane Austen. Timeless and unmistakably authentic in its unique lens into girlhood, Extra Geography is a lasting addition to the growing canon movies about female friendships. —Tomris Laffly

2026-family-dinner.title: Family Dinner
2026-family-dinner.summary: Dinner conversation at the table of a most imaginative family who definitely do not subscribe to the old saying, “Never play with your food!”

2026-fatherland.title: Fatherland
2026-fatherland.summary: Play Trailer Polish filmmaker Pawel Pawlikowski (MVFF41 Tribute) continues his ongoing examination of the emotional wounds and ruins of postwar Europe with this indelible drama. Joining the poetic ranks of his Oscar®-winning Ida (2013) and Oscar-nominated Cold War (MVFF41) in an unofficial trilogy, his latest black-and-white elegy traces the relationship between renowned writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his accomplished actress-writer daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, among the finest performers working today), across a lyrical journey in a fractured Germany of 1949 where the exiled Mann is to receive the Goethe Prize. It’s the height of the Cold War, and the land that carries the duo’s roots is both deeply divided and consumed by unspoken guilt. A reflective and unforgettable study of identity, family, and national memory, Fatherland is simply a stunner in effortlessly braiding the makings of a classical road movie with an artistic statement on generational remorse. —Tomris Laffly

2026-filthy.title: Filthy
2026-filthy.summary: A teenager preparing for a “purity ball” faces some harsh realities about religious expectation, self-worth, and personal expression.

2026-fjord.title: Fjord
2026-fjord.summary: Play Trailer Winning his second Palme d’Or after 2007’s chilling masterwork 4 Months, 3 Weeks, and 2 Days , Romanian writer-director Cristian Mungiu delivers one of the most urgent movies of the year. And he does so through a query both timeless and of today: Is there a world in which we can be free of biases when pursuing truth and justice, or are we always a little blindsided by our belief systems? The audience will certainly wonder and self-interrogate in following Mungiu’s atmospheric legal thriller about a devout religious couple with ambiguous values (superstars Renate Reinsve and Sebastian Stan, both brilliant and against type) and their five children, disrupted by Norway’s inflexible child protection laws. An incisive courtroom procedural and a searing family drama that refreshingly checks all forms of moral pandering at the door, Mungiu’s latest is as cool, imposing, and silently deep as the fjord that lends this gorgeous enigma its backdrop. —Tomris Laffly

2026-flesh-impact.title: Flesh Impact
2026-flesh-impact.summary: Director Maggie Gyllenhaal tells a revisionist history of Marilyn Monroe (Dakota Johnson, Ellen Burstyn), who faces down studio pressure to assert her voice and influence, in a speculation on a career that might have been.

2026-free-joan-little.title: Free Joan Little
2026-free-joan-little.summary: Award-winning filmmaker Yoruba Richen excavates a groundbreaking true-life 1975 case that galvanized Black Power activists, feminists, and prison reformers around one young Black woman’s historic fight for justice and the right to defend herself against sexual violence.

2026-giants-do-fall.title: Giants Do Fall
2026-giants-do-fall.summary: It’s a classic David vs. Goliath scenario: A group of fed-up, alarmed citizens, living on key stretches of land in Louisiana and Appalachia's Rust Belt where factory pollution and fracking have become de rigueur, square off against big business and politicos. The mobilized and impassioned group prove to be a formidable foe, demanding answers and accountability as they find themselves thrust into a role they never imagined they’d play: accidental activists. Giants Do Fall relates the devastating personal toll incurred by communities near petrochemical factories and fracking sites, and also how historical racism and corruption reflect another facet of these environmental disasters. Beyond that, Megan Ponder and Stiv Wilson’s documentary serves as an inspirational testament to the collective power and might ordinary citizens can wield when they unite around a common cause to protect what they cherish and hold dear. —Randy Myers

2026-goddamn-s-great-big-adventure-the-d.title: Goddamn's Great Big Adventure: The Dating Crisis!!
2026-goddamn-s-great-big-adventure-the-d.summary: Adorable little Goddamn is ready for love but where is that obscure object of desire

2026-gravity.title: Gravity
2026-gravity.summary: Twelve-year old Deniz finds that being a girl changes dynamics among her boy schoolmates in her small rural town.

2026-grow-up.title: Grow Up
2026-grow-up.summary: When 12-year-old Kai realizes his older brother has outgrown their childhood games, he decides it's time to grow up too, though he's unsure if he's ready.

2026-happiness-for-a-herder.title: Happiness for a Herder
2026-happiness-for-a-herder.summary: Free-spirited and expressive, Charlie Eguia’s Happiness for a Herder follows a group of nomadic herder families in Mongolia.

2026-happy-birthday.title: Happy Birthday
2026-happy-birthday.summary: Two delighted eight-year-olds wake up in the middle of the night to excitedly prepare for a birthday party. They might be sisters, or best friends, or cousins. The drama brilliantly demurs in giving us clarity, until the film’s focus settles on Toha (a phenomenal Doha Ramadan), already a maid at such a young age. What unfolds are her poignant experiences as she navigates the dramatic class differences between her own family and that of her employers and their world of privilege. Set in contemporary Cairo, the incomparable Ramadan conveys the force of a little girl’s will to resist the small injustices she does not fully comprehend. Writer-director Sarah Goher’s surprising and heartbreaking film, a beautifully written and photographed story of resilience, will leave you contemplating what it means to grow up too fast when circumstance is the cruelest master of all. —Topiary Landberg

2026-happy-portrait.title: Happy Portrait
2026-happy-portrait.summary: In this fun musical homage to the toons of the 1940s, a struggling artist can’t seem to get his self-portrait on canvas until his paints and brushes come to the rescue.

2026-harvest-party-at-camp-two.title: Harvest Party at Camp Two
2026-harvest-party-at-camp-two.summary: It is 1980 in Yuba City, California in Reaa Puri’s Harvest Party At Camp Two , and a group of Young Punjabi Sikh farmworkers throw the biggest party their small town has ever seen.

2026-x.title: Κράτα Με
2026-x.summary: Play Trailer Winner of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival’s World Cinema Audience Award, Myrsini Aristodou’s sensitive debut resonates with deeply felt authenticity and lasting emotional power. Precocious 11-year-old Iris is used to being on her own. Left alone while her mother vacations with a boyfriend and ignored by her peers, Iris distracts herself by doing what she does best: getting into trouble. When local law enforcement detains her, an unforeseen figure emerges to bail her out, the father she has never known. Though his interests appear selfish, they bond through a shared talent for scams and desire for connection, beginning a delicate dance of testing trust and discovering each other. With an exquisite eye for detail and the confident casting of expressive Maria Petrova, a non-actor, in the role of Iris, Aristodou balances fragility and longing with effortless control, announcing herself not just as a filmmaker to watch, but one worthy of awe. —Landon Zakheim

2026-hot-spring-therapy.title: Hot Spring Therapy
2026-hot-spring-therapy.summary: A snow monkey bathing in a natural hot spring has an out-of-body experience and requires some well-trained snowflakes to revive him with their magical powers.

2026-i-love-my-guts.title: I Love My Guts
2026-i-love-my-guts.summary: After being dumped, a teenage girl literally spills her guts, dragging her entrails through school and family dinners in search of someone who cares.

2026-ikari.title: Ikari
2026-ikari.summary: Sibling creatures snuggle and struggle to find their own place and space from—and with—each other.

2026-i-m-stuck-in-a-mascot-suit-in-anoth.title: I'm Stuck in a Mascot Suit in Another World
2026-i-m-stuck-in-a-mascot-suit-in-anoth.summary: The humorous story of a man working as a teddy bear mascot who gets transported to a land of plush animals where the humans live in cages and stuffies rule the world.

2026-in-chiapas.title: In Chiapas
2026-in-chiapas.summary: Memories of one man’s literal and figurative trip to Chiapas accompanied by his brother and a bag of magic mushrooms soaked in honey.

2026-in-her-you-ll-find-sanctuary.title: In Her You'll Find Sanctuary
2026-in-her-you-ll-find-sanctuary.summary: Two young nuns embark on a holier-than-thou competition that evokes some heavy emotions.

2026-in-waves.title: In Waves
2026-in-waves.summary: Play Trailer Some things arrive in waves: sunlight, joy, the pounding surf, but also loss and grief. Director Phuong Mai Nguyen’s animated adaptation of AJ Dungo’s award-winning 2019 graphic novel unfolds as a story of young love between two teenagers: AJ, a shy skateboarder and aspiring artist (voiced by Will Sharpe), and Kristen (Stephanie Hsu), a self-confident surfer. The usual fears of parental reproach and peer pressure challenge their growing intimacy that is further tested by the emergence of a life-threatening illness. Nguyen’s exquisite visual sensibility is on display on multiple levels: through the vibrant colors of present-day SoCal life, the black-and-white line drawings from AJ’s sketchbooks, and the soft tones of an imagined past life among a group of native Hawai’ians living at the water’s edge. A soundtrack from French composers Oklou and ROB beautifully complements the imagery to an exquisitely indelible effect. —KD Davis

2026-le-corset.title: Le Corset
2026-le-corset.summary: Play Trailer Christophe is just on the cusp of adolescence, working every day on his family’s financially embattled farm. There is love between him and his distant father, his tougher older brother, pixiesh baby sister, and long-suffering mother, but when balance issues require that Christophe wear an iron corset 24/7, his life goes into a tailspin and makes him an outcast. Two people come to his rescue: a middle-aged church musician who encourages him to play the organ, and a Huck Finn-like female schoolmate who teaches him to take risks and gives him his first hilariously unexpected kiss. Director Louis Clichy, an animator on Wall-E and Up , employs delicate hand-drawn watercolor imagery and casts his son Gary as Chrisophe’s voice, in this feature co-written with Frank Salome. With Iron Boy , Clichy delivers a tender, funny rite-of-passage story that honestly confronts the distress that every adolescent endures. —Larry Gross

2026-isabel.title: Isabel
2026-isabel.summary: Play Trailer Isabel (Marina Person) knows wine, but she knows even better what she does not want: another day working for a demanding boss who treats wine as business rather than pleasure. Dreaming of opening her own natural wine bar, she begins navigating the unpredictable territory between desiring a different life and making it happen. Gabe Klinger finds humor, melancholy, and unexpected pleasures in Isabel's attempts to take control of her future, creating a warm and engaging portrait of a woman who keeps moving even when things don't go according to plan. Set in São Paulo's lively wine and restaurant scene, the city becomes an essential part of the story, captured on gorgeous, grainy 16mm film. Marina Person, who also collaborated on the screenplay, gives a wonderfully charismatic performance as Isabel, full of wit, determination, and humanity. With its great soundtrack, vibrant art direction, and love for life's imperfect pleasures, Isabel is an inviting toast to starting over. — João Federici

2026-italiano.title: Italiano
2026-italiano.summary: A gay couple reevaluates their relationship to their repressive Persian culture when the prospect of leaving their homeland arises.

2026-it-s-a-wonderful-night-of-the-livin.title: It's a Wonderful Night of the Living Dead
2026-it-s-a-wonderful-night-of-the-livin.summary: John and Dan Bell’s It’s a Wonderful Night of the Living Dead is an irresistible mashup of Frank Capra and George Romero.

2026-it-s-my-fault.title: It's My Fault
2026-it-s-my-fault.summary: A 14-year-old boy collects stones on an ordinary day, one from his drunken mother and another from a street fight he was too scared to stop.

2026-jail-time-records.title: Jail Time Records
2026-jail-time-records.summary: Traveling through an overcrowded prison labyrinth in Douala, Cameroon, you’ll find a mercurial village full of petty thieves, murderers, and political scapegoats. A New Bell Prison ‘barker’ winds us through a chaotic din of bullies, hagglers, and sleepers, past guards pumping iron, into a closet-sized sanctuary where something magical happens. This is Jail Time Records, a music label founded by the film’s co-directors, former prisoner Steve Happi and his partner, Dione Roach. What began as an in-house recording studio is now a vital platform for artists—both incarcerated and free—using music to forge second chances amid poverty, corruption, and an overburdened judicial system. This directorial debut is unlike most prison documentaries, moving between the grit of daily survival and sudden bursts of rap, song, and dance, creating a shared stage of extraordinary expression. The label may not be able to engineer freedom from systemic failure, but it does offer hope for redemption and a different future for those who want it. Winner of three top prizes at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival: Best Documentary Feature, Albert Maysles Award for Best New Documentary, and Best Cinematography in a Documentary Feature - Michelle Svenson

2026-jean-michel-basquiat.title: Jean-Michel Basquiat
2026-jean-michel-basquiat.summary: Jean-Michel Basquiat burned brightly in his 27 years—and still does in a legacy both artistic and personal reflected in this touching and at turns heartbreaking and buoyant documentary (the only one officially approved by Basquiat’s estate and family) centered around reminiscences by the painter’s surviving sisters, Lisane and Jeanine. The siblings relate stories of life at home in the family’s Brooklyn brownstone, their brother’s early interest in drawing, and the difficulties that arose when their parents separated. To augment these memories and catalog his rise in the art world, the film employs exceptional archival footage and key voices of contemporaries, including Fab 5 Freddy, Kenny Scharf, and Arthur Jafa. As these artists express what Basquiat meant to them and to the downtown NYC demimonde, Lisane and Jeanine speak to how affable, kind, gregarious, and flawed their sibling was. The result is very much a multidimensional portrait of the artist, but even more, the portrait of an endlessly fascinating man. Winner, Best Editing in a Documentary Feature, 2026 Tribeca Film Festival. —Rod Armstrong

guests.role: Director | Recipient of the MVFF Bay Area Rising Star Award | Elton Creation Special Jury Prize

2026-la-gradiva.title: La Gradiva
2026-la-gradiva.summary: Play Trailer French teenagers take a summer class trip to Naples, Italy, in this marvelous coming-of-age film, which garnered the Cannes Critics Week Best Picture award for first-time feature filmmaker Marine Atlan and her co-writer Anne Brouillet. The focus is on three kids—gorgeous rich-kid seducer James (Mitia Capellier-Audat), his charismatic but angry buddy Toni (Colas Quignard), and shy but observant nerdy outsider Suzanne (Suzanne Gerin) —and their teacher Mercier (Antonia Buresi). It’s hard to convey how subtle, mysterious, and completely intelligent this drama is—a dark but never dour or depressing investigation of the perils of adolescent fantasizing about sexual romance and family history, as well as the enduring effects of class antagonism and resentment. It’s a drama that conveys 2026’s complete sexual fluidity: Everyone is androgynous to a greater or lesser degree, and everyone is both promiscuous and frightened in unexpected ways. With marvelous sundrenched Italian landscapes photographed by Pierre Mazoyer and Atlan, a controlled ironic tone, and a superb ensemble. La Gradiva is one of the most assured directorial debuts in years. —Larry Gross

2026-lady.title: Lady
2026-lady.summary: Filmed in the chaotic streets of Lagos, Nigeria, Olive Nwosu's first feature is a striking neo-noir that crackles with tension. One of the traffic-choked city’s few female cab drivers, Lady is independent, isolated, and mistrustful, surviving by staying laser-focused on her own business. Her foundation is shaken by the sudden reappearance of Pinky, the sister-like childhood friend who abandoned Lady years ago and became a sex worker. Tempted by the promise of money, time with Pinky, and a possible path out of a nation on the brink of political and social combustion, Lady reluctantly accepts a job driving Pinky’s crew of glamorous, reckless coworkers through the dangerous netherworld of Lagos nightlife. Writer-director Nwosu, fresh among Africa’s new wave of auteurs, shines with her debut. The cast, which won the Special Jury Award for Acting Ensemble at Sundance, is phenomenal, crafting a moving portrayal of the unexpected sisterhood that finally breaches Lady’s armor. —D. Quinones

guests.role: Host of You Must Remember This, Podcast

2026-little-green-men-quip-s-in-charge.title: Little Green Men: Quip's in Charge
2026-little-green-men-quip-s-in-charge.summary: When the Empress transports herself to a spa planet for some much-needed R&R, her assistant Quip takes charge for the day and has some ambitious plans.

2026-love-of-your-life.title: Love of Your Life
2026-love-of-your-life.summary: When career nurse Mimi (Margaret Qualley, Blue Moon MVFF48) finds the love of her life, it's exhilarating, profound, and wonderfully crazy. But as things are upturned by the pandemic, all bets are off. Qualley and director Rachel Morrison (MTG Award 2025, The Fire Inside ) explore the uncharted emotional territory facing Mimi as she abruptly leaves home and cuts herself off from the life she’s known, even long-time best friend Jason (Patrick Schwarzenegger). Over time, she travels to Portugal and—after an interlude with Felix (Aaron Pierre) begins to soften her heart—onward to London. Morrison’s fluid storytelling takes us on a journey both geographic and emotional that takes place over several years and locations before Mimi returns to the East Coast. One of the first films to explore the emotional landscape of the effects of the pandemic, it’s a story that dives beneath the surface of feelings and experiences that are uplifting and heartbreaking, challenging and sometimes just messy—and are deeply relatable. —Zoë Elton CAFILM MEMBERS ONLY SCREENING Monday, Oct. 5 • 5:00 PM. Free, but ticket required After the screening, take a short stroll across the street to the Outdoor Art Club for a Members Only Reception!

2026-making-space.title: Making Space
2026-making-space.summary: Azorel, a dog-like urban dweller, navigates a fantastical reimagined city that explores how we reshape spaces to reflect our communities.

2026-mamalonacitos.title: Mamalonacitos
2026-mamalonacitos.summary: Watch out, LA—the badass mamalonacitas are coming to a mall near you and they’re taking no prisoners!

2026-minotaure.title: Minotaure
2026-minotaure.summary: The year is 2022 and the backdrop is Putin’s corruption-drenched Russia in LEVIATHAN Oscar-nominee Andrey Zvyagintsev’s latest, his first feature in a decade after 2017’s astounding LOVELESS. A bone-chilling reimagining of both Claude Chabrol’s LA FEMME INFIDELE and Adrian Lyne’s UNFAITHFUL, Zvyagintsev’s own thriller follows the essentials of the source material: amid various work pressures, a powerful businessman (Dmitriy Mazurov) learns that his increasingly distant wife (Iris Lebedeva) is cheating on him. But the filmmaker also puts a masterfully nihilistic spin on the story’s machinations, wondering, with his ingenious inquisitiveness and observantly still camerawork, if any authority in his motherland would care about unspeakable acts of crime when the country is at war with Ukraine, and a sense of lawlessness has seized the higher-ups. The winner of the Grand Prix prize at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, MINOTAUR gifts us a parting note that feels like a silent scream with echoes that inhabit the soul. -- Tomris Laffly

2026-miriam.title: Miriam
2026-miriam.summary: With an experimental sensibility, Karla Condado’s Miriam copes with grief as the filmmaker reads personal letters to her aunt who was a victim of femicide.

2026-miss-representation-rise-up.title: Miss Representation: Rise Up
2026-miss-representation-rise-up.summary: Play Trailer A hostile environment confronts girls online with every scroll, click, and swipe. In this digital landscape, relentless harassment, manipulated content, and deepfakes target their mental health, privacy, and self-esteem, while algorithms actively steer young men toward an aggressive online "manosphere" that normalizes anti-female hostility. Serving as a follow-up to Jennifer Siebel Newsom's 2011 documentary Miss Representation , this film brings together emerging female voices with insights from leaders including Hillary Clinton, Nancy Pelosi, Amy Klobuchar, and Gretchen Carlson. Together, they expose how technology, politics, and corporate decision-making fuel a digital culture where misogyny continues to thrive. Ultimately, the film amplifies the voices of women demanding accountability from governments and tech companies while safeguarding the future of the next generation of female leaders. —Michelle Svenson

2026-musk.title: Musk
2026-musk.summary: Play Trailer Elon Musk’s remarks—that it’s possible our contemporary reality is actually a computer simulated video game designed by a superior intelligence—inspired veteran filmmaker Alex Gibney in making this epic, four-hour documentary about the mercurial billionaire. Gibney focuses on Musk’s early success as a Silicon Valley start-up whiz and how he took financial control of Tesla while exaggerating his role in designing it, but also gives us the genuinely impressive story of the evolution of SpaceX. The darker side involves Musk’s brutally callous treatment of the many women who bore his children, and the way his paranoia about criminal liability drove him to become one of the most powerful power brokers in right-wing politics. When Gibney gets to the DOGE phase of Musk’s career and his alliance with Donald Trump, he confirms his starting thesis by demonstrating how the aesthetics of videogame reality are the best model for Musk’s approach to restructuring the United States government. Musk is now the wealthiest person in human history, and Gibney shows how the spreading influence of AI gives Musk unparalleled power to collect data on any and every person on this planet. This cumulative portrait of Elon Musk is dispassionate, mesmerizingly complex, and terrifying. —Larry Gross

2026-my-mother-told-me-not-to-talk-to-st.title: My Mother Told Me Not to Talk to... Strangers
2026-my-mother-told-me-not-to-talk-to-st.summary: A young girl's ordinary afternoon at the park leads to an unexpected connection with a stranger that gradually reveals an unsettling undercurrent between trust and danger.

2026-my-undesirable-friends-part-ii-exil.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile
2026-my-undesirable-friends-part-ii-exil.summary: Play Trailer At the close of the five-and-a-half hour My Undesirable Friends: Part I—Last Air in Moscow , the last remaining holdouts of non-state news media in Russia were driven into exile. Already labeled “foreign agents,” harassed, jailed, and sometimes killed, they fled the country within days of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. This likewise iPhone-shot, epic, and thrillingly urgent sequel records their fates since. The largely young female protagonists scatter first to Istanbul, then throughout Europe and beyond. Officially banned at home, stubbornly independent TV Rain persists in reaching millions of Russians from a new HQ in Latvia, even as constantly shifting politics imperil every refuge. Meanwhile, spies, threats, poisoning, further forced relocations, long-distance liquidation of personal assets, and other bitter pills constitute these brave colleagues’ reminders of “home.” Nonetheless, they keep reporting truths whose expression could exact the ultimate price...even as other nations (including our own) edge towards free-press crackdowns. —Dennis Harvey

2026-no-hands-the-wild-ride-of-the-schwi.title: No Hands: The Wild Ride of the Schwinn Bicycle Company
2026-no-hands-the-wild-ride-of-the-schwi.summary: No Hands: The Wild Ride of the Schwinn Bicycle Company is exactly that. It's a wild ride about an enduring American brand; it's a history of our nation, of the world, and of a family throughout the last century. This testament to the endurance of the American dream, narrated by Lance Armstrong, is both nostalgic and edifying — a unique look at how one company's fortunes rose and fell alongside the country's own — but the film really shines when the spotlight turns to a group of Marin County mountain bikers à la Robin Williams who screech onto the scene, kicking up dust and showing us how the real ruff-riders roll. This is a local film with international insight that'll have you getting misty over banana seats or eyeing that old 10-speed out in the garage and fantasizing about riding it down the south side of Mount Tam. —Claire Holl

2026-noodle-fight.title: Noodle Fight
2026-noodle-fight.summary: A girlfight at poolside between two frenemies who both emerge triumphant.

2026-normal-glasses.title: Normal Glasses
2026-normal-glasses.summary: Can’t a girl just get a pair of regular old glasses in the astral plane?

2026-odyssey.title: Odyssey
2026-odyssey.summary: What if the United States hadn't pulled the plug on Apollo, as Apple's For All Mankind imagined? Built from 2,500 hours of restored archival footage, director Avi Belkin masterfully constructs a riveting thriller around the fateful Apollo 13 mission. Unfolding through the intimate perspective of astronaut Jim Lovell and his family, and executive produced by Tom Hanks, the film tracks his lunar dreams to that distressing message: "Houston, we've had a problem." Driven by a stark, chilling sci-fi score that pulsates from the vacuum of the cosmos to a frantic Mission Control, a united planet holds its breath as geopolitical divisions briefly recede—a fragile unity the real Apollo program wouldn't outlive. A country fractured by Vietnam, social unrest, anti-science sentiment, and mounting costs shuttered America's lunar program soon after Odyssey's splashdown. Half a century on, a new Space Race of global powers and private titans has turned our eyes back to the Moon, leaving us to ponder: What if we'd never stopped? -Michelle Svenson

2026-of-veins-and-wires.title: Of Veins and Wires
2026-of-veins-and-wires.summary: Of Veins and Wires imagines a future where artificial means can replace human procreation.

2026-once-upon-a-time-in-harlem.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
2026-once-upon-a-time-in-harlem.summary: Play Trailer It is a film we thought we’d never get to see: a documentary culled from footage shot by Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One director William Greaves in August 1972 of the surviving members of the Harlem Renaissance, all gathered together at Duke Ellington’s New York apartment to reminisce about and debate their movement’s legacy. At long last, Greaves’ son David completes his late father’s passion project, 50-year-old footage becoming 2026’s signature cinematic event. Once Upon a Time in Harlem is a tapestry of intimate, electric conversation between actors, writers, and others who helped shape the creative flowering of Black artists in the 1920s and ‘30s. But what’s remarkable—and also sobering—is how much of their exchanges touch on the racism and economic inequality still plaguing America in the 21st century. Much like the Oscar®-winning Summer of Soul , this nearly forgotten hangout brings history alive and emerges as a vital cultural landmark. It’s a party like no other—one full of brilliant personalities and bracing ideas. —Tim Grierson

2026-oppression.title: Oppression
2026-oppression.summary: Inspired by Langston Hughes' poem, this film uses a bird as metaphor to confront the devastating reality in Palestine, refusing to let viewers look away.

2026-out-of-the-blue.title: Out of the Blue
2026-out-of-the-blue.summary: When six-year-old actress Emily grows distressed on set, revealing unexpected childhood trauma, the director must balance her safety and agency with keeping the production alive.
