2026-poetry.title: Poetry
2026-poetry.summary: Play Trailer A frail woman in her mid-60s, Mi-ja (Yun Jeong-hie) is raising her teenage son Jong-wook (Lee Da-wit), and works as a housekeeper and nurse to bitter, bedridden Mr. Kang (Kim Hee-ra). In the film’s first movement, she faces two catastrophes, beginning with a doctor’s visit that reveals she’s suffering from early onset Alzheimer's. Rather than tell anyone, Mi-ja registers in an amateur poetry class. Then she discovers Jong-wook was among a group that raped a classmate, leading to her suicide. To keep the boys out of prison, a bribe must be paid to the victim’s poverty-stricken mother, but Mi-ja lacks the money to pay her share. As these two crises develop, she continues to work on writing a single poem. In lesser hands, all this could have easily turned into something overly sappy and cloying. But with his fifth feature, writer/director Lee Chang-dong eludes those risks, thanks to Yun’s luminous, often funny performance and his own uncanny gift for staging scenes with dispassionate, often wordless, subtlety. Both a lament for the frailty of human lives and a celebration of our insatiable appetite for creativity and beauty, Poetry is exquisite. —Larry Gross

guests.role: Director | Recipient of the MVFF Auteur Director Award

2026-purge.title: Purge
2026-purge.summary: A week after her mother's death, Jiho forgets it entirely as her inner self, "Thought," demands she purge every trace while Jiho clings to denial.

2026-pylons.title: Pylons
2026-pylons.summary: What happens when what you thought you wanted no longer fulfills. Should you take that giant leap into the unknown?

2026-queen-at-sea.title: Queen at Sea
2026-queen-at-sea.summary: Play Trailer What happens when love is no longer enough to protect someone you care for? Amanda (Juliette Binoche), already struggling with her own life, finds herself at the center of an impossible family dilemma. Her mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) is living with advanced dementia, while her devoted stepfather Martin (Tom Courtenay) refuses to accept that their intimate life must come to an end. When Amanda calls the authorities, a deeply private question becomes a matter for the police, carers, and institutions, setting the family on a path none of them can control. Sara (Florence Hunt), Amanda’s teenage daughter, brings another perspective as three generations of women navigate very different stages of love, desire, independence, and loss. Writer/director Lance Hammer handles this delicate subject with remarkable restraint, never offering easy answers or clear heroes or villains. The central trio finds humor, tenderness, frustration, and love in the smallest moments. Winner of the Berlinale Silver Bear Jury Prize, Queen at Sea also earned Silver Bears for Anna Calder-Marshall and Tom Courtenay. —João Federici

2026-querida-fatima.title: Querida Fátima
2026-querida-fatima.summary: Play Trailer A decade after the murder of her 12-year-old daughter, Lorena Gutiérrez refuses to let Fátima's story disappear. Camping outside Mexico's National Palace, she waits for an audience with the country's first female president, carrying a question that has nagged at Lorena for years: What does justice look like when nothing can bring back your child? Lorena is among the directors of this documentary that transforms personal grief into a deeply intimate act of remembrance and resistance. The film moves between Lorena's recollections, her family's struggle, and the stories of other mothers who have also lost daughters to violence, creating a portrait that is as much about love and memory as it is about the search for accountability. Most importantly, Fátima emerges as no mere statistic, but as a girl with dreams, a daughter remembered with tenderness and determination. This triple Guadalajara International Film Festival award winner is a powerful testament to a mother who never imagined becoming an activist but found in that fight a way to keep her daughter's memory alive. - João Federici

2026-x-2.title: تمرین‌هایی برای یک انقلاب
2026-x-2.summary: Play Trailer Filmmaking seems to run through Pegah Ahangarani’s veins. Her parents are both noted for their work behind the camera, while she’s been a screen actor since childhood, finding stardom at age 15 in 1999’s The Girl in the Sneakers . But in this unique decades-spanning nonfiction, the focus is not on professional history, but on the collision between personal and political spheres. Assembled entirely from preexisting footage and errata, it charts the often-cruel fates of immediate family, relatives, and mentors from before the 1979 Iranian Revolution—which many hoped would bring liberation—through successive crackdowns on dissent under the Islamic Republic. Some ultimately fled the country; others were less fortunate. Complete with harrowing glimpses from the midst of protests violently quelled by police, this first-person account laments a homeland that’s suffered under authoritarian control for the now-exiled director’s entire life. It’s a graceful tally of serial rebellions and disillusionments that won Cannes’ Golden Eye award this spring. —Dennis Harvey

2026-rogue-one-a-star-wars-story.title: Rogue One a Star Wars Story

2026-room-of-the-absolute.title: Room of the Absolute
2026-room-of-the-absolute.summary: A collaboration between Ukrainian painter Alla Hurenko and directors Natalie Shirinian and Elizabeth Baudouin, Room of the Absolute is a time capsule and portrait of resilience in the face of relentless destruction in Ukraine.

2026-rose.title: Rose
2026-rose.summary: Play Trailer In the village, they call him a soldier, as well as an outsider and a misfit. Concealing many secrets and a facial scar, he excels at hard work in his quest to become part of the community. But beneath the soldier’s identity is a woman discovering a new sense of freedom and independence by living as a man, possibilities that would otherwise be denied to her. Sandra Hüller ( Anatomy of a Fall , MVFF46) delivers a performance of searing psychological intensity as a 17th-century war veteran. Markus Schleinzer’s third feature, after Michael and Angelo , is a stark historical drama; its striking black-and-white imagery reinforces its questions about gender, identity, and the price of belonging, revealing how simply being perceived as a man can open doors otherwise closed to women. Formally stunning and visually painterly, this human and deeply unsettling portrait turns a historical story into a provocative reflection on freedom, identity, and the lengths we go to claim our own lives. —Ivonne Cotorruelo

2026-arru.title: Árru
2026-arru.summary: Play Trailer In this inventive, visually arresting directorial debut from indigenous Sámi filmmaker Elle Sofe Sara, we follow Maia (Sara Marielle Gaup Beaska), a Sámi reindeer herder whose livelihood and ancestral lands are under imminent threat by an upcoming mining project. As a last-ditch effort, she contacts her estranged uncle for legal advice. But his return to their Sápmi home in Europe’s icy far north reopens deep familial wounds, and Maia faces an impossible choice of what to protect: her family or the land they rely upon to survive. The first ever feature film to do so, Árru weaves the joik , a traditional form of Sámi music, into the drama’s narrative, creating a singular, breathtaking audio-visual experience that brings Sámi culture to the big screen in a bold new way. —Sofia Felino

2026-chicas-tristes.title: Chicas Tristes
2026-chicas-tristes.summary: Fernanda Tovar, in her narrative debut feature, winner of the Crystal Bear for Best Film in the Generation 14plus at the Berlinale, crafts a moving coming-of-age drama about friendship, teenage girlhood, and trauma. Rocio Guzmán gives a standout performance as La Maestra scraping by as best she can to understand how to be a good ally to her friend Paula (Darana Álvarez). Friends and swimmers Paula and La Maestra navigate life with the same confidence they show in the pool. Dreams cast a quiet spell over the early stretches of the film, though its premonitory title, Sad Girlz , suggests that the girls’ carefree world will not remain untouched. One night when they go to a party, something happens to Paula. As their journey deepens and complicates their bond, these two remarkable young women provide a sense of warmth that makes Sad Girlz linger in the heart long after the credits roll. —Ivonne Cotorruelo MVFF49 Mind the Gap Creation Prize Winner

2026-scissors.title: Scissors
2026-scissors.summary: A moving tale of three generations of Chinese women whose dreams and struggles are linked by one pair of scissors.

2026-scout-s-honor.title: Scout's Honor
2026-scout-s-honor.summary: In Isabel Pask’s comedic short, selling girl scout cookies is a hidden path for two friends to achieve a much larger goal…or so they think.

2026-seagull-coffee.title: Seagull Coffee
2026-seagull-coffee.summary: A little girl accompanies her mom to the café where she works and discovers a seagull with undiscovered barista talents.

2026-self-titled.title: Self-Titled
2026-self-titled.summary: Actor Morena Baccarin ( Firefly ) makes her directing debut with this tale about the lessons a young girl learns from her father over the years, and how they resonate in her unknown future.

2026-silly-little-plastic-cat.title: Silly Little Plastic Cat
2026-silly-little-plastic-cat.summary: Along the picturesque coastline of Brittany, France, bright orange novelty Garfield phones wash ashore in Zack Grant’s eccentric short.

2026-plitsch-platsch-forever.title: Plitsch Platsch Forever!
2026-plitsch-platsch-forever.summary: Play Trailer Pre-teens Pola and Polly are inseparable friends who spend the long summer days at Splish Splash, the local pool, where Polly’s mom runs the concession stand. When the pool shuts down for lengthy repairs, Polly’s family departs Switzerland for Canada in search of steady work, leaving Pola heartbroken about losing her BFF and angry at her village for closing the coolest spot in town. With the help of Rosalie, the smartest (and geekiest) girl in her class, Pola plots to reopen Splish Splash, recruiting friends—and former enemies—to her side. Her grassroots-style civic activism goes all the way to the top, and even Mayor Petrović-Stucki can’t get the girls off her back or out of her office. Featuring some wildly creative costumes, musical dance numbers, and fabulous young talent, Splish Splash Forever! is an upbeat and infectiously inspiring story of activism, kid-style, and the enduring power of friendship. —KD Davis In German with English subtitles. Appropriate for grades 5-8 (ages 10-13)

2026-stand-alone.title: Stand Alone
2026-stand-alone.summary: Snakes slide along the frame, doing their beautiful dance of life.

2026-sticker.title: Sticker
2026-sticker.summary: A poor little sticker is tired of being stuck to a notebook, so he hitches a ride for a wider view of the world.

2026-storybook-apocalypse-or-the-ship-s-.title: Storybook Apocalypse (Or, The Ship's Cat)
2026-storybook-apocalypse-or-the-ship-s-.summary: A beautifully told first-person account of a youthful stowaway who finds solace and companionship with the ship’s cat.

2026-superspice.title: Superspice
2026-superspice.summary: A humorous punk-rock high school drama centering on an undying craving for an elusive incendiary snack.

2026-swimming-the-colorado-naked.title: Swimming the Colorado Naked
2026-swimming-the-colorado-naked.summary: A young man challenges himself to swim across a freezing river, only to discover the error of his ways when he gets to the opposite shore.

2026-swing-swish-sway.title: Swing Swish Sway
2026-swing-swish-sway.summary: TT Takemoto's colorful and tangible reconstruction of history is inspired by Filipina-American Rose Bamberger, founder of Daughters of Bilitis, San Francisco’s own first lesbian activist group.

2026-tangles.title: Tangles
2026-tangles.summary: “My mom is awesome!” exclaims young Sarah about her mom, Midge. From a daughter’s memories of her mother wielding her flashlight like a lightsaber as she vanquished nighttime demons lurking in Sarah’s bedroom; to winter walks in the Maine woods, stealing maple sap from the tree farm; through Sarah’s adolescence, coming out as queer, with Midge marching alongside her at LGBTQ+ rallies—awesomeness to the bone. Then things get tangled: small changes of behavior, easy to dismiss at first (“it’s just menopause”) until the signs are too evident to ignore. Leah Nelson’s beautifully rendered animated film, based on Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir ( Tangles: A Story About Alzheimer’s, My Mother and Me ), stars Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Abbi Jacobson, Samira Wiley, Bryan Cranston, Beanie Feldstein, Wanda Sykes, and Seth Rogen voicing Sarah’s lovingly tangled extended family, struggling to support each other as one of them slips away too fast. —KD Davis

2026-tender-loving-care.title: Tender Loving Care
2026-tender-loving-care.summary: Following Hard Truths (MVFF47), legendary auteur Mike Leigh returns with another tragicomic look at modern life filled with compelling characters and sharp social commentary. Following a nasty breakup, Amy ( Widow’s Bay breakout Kate O’Flynn) packs up her life and moves back in with Rosie (Alice Bailey Johnson), her lifelong best friend and colleague in social work. Through visits with their diverse array of clients and Amy’s aging parents (Marion Bailey and Paul Jesson), the two women grapple with precarious work-life balance, burnout, and many shades of heartbreak…but nothing a nice glass of wine can’t fix. Tender Loving Care is a powerful meditation on the nature of compassion: who we decide is deserving of care, if and how we can help those who refuse it, and the dear costs paid by those we expect to spend it freely. —Sofia Felino

2026-tenzing.title: Tenzing
2026-tenzing.summary: Play Trailer When Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) ascends the summit of Mount Everest in 1953, the first person to do so, he is not alone. With him is climbing partner Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a Nepalese guide and veteran of expeditions to reach the top. Documentary filmmaker Jennifer Peedom’s ( Sherpa , Mountain ) first narrative feature relates the story of a loving husband and father who was never accepted by the European teams or the local Sherpa clans, but who navigated both cliques and cultures to become an essential element in achieving mountaineering’s greatest milestone. Amidst the epic Himalayan landscapes, every crevasse, every impossible face, and every blizzard presents a life-or-death scenario that Tenzing meets with patience, serenity, and love for the mountain in whose shadow he’s lived for decades. Willem Dafoe adds robust support as Colonel John Hunt, the head of the British expedition team. —Sterling Hedgpeth

2026-the-a-word-the-future-of-aging.title: The A-Word: The Future of Aging
2026-the-a-word-the-future-of-aging.summary: Play Trailer We’re all familiar with those slick hucksters hawking magical anti-aging elixirs they claim will extend lives and make us look and feel younger. Few, if any, work. Today, though, sees a new dawn emerging as vetted research scientists and innovators—some entrenched in the Bay Area—make significant breakthroughs that have the potential to add “quality” years to our lives. Greg Kohs, award-winning director of the 2008 documentary Song Sung Blue that inspired the 2025 Kate Hudson-Hugh Jackman film, explores exciting gains made in the biotech world and introduces us to groundbreakers making that happen, including San Francisco’s Celine Halioua, CEO/founder of a biotech startup that’s championing longevity medication that’s being tested on dogs. Kohs juxtaposes these encouraging developments with poignant testimonies from a close-knit community of residents in Maine whose stories suggest a positive outlook, an active lifestyle, and animal companions are key to making an extended lifespan worth living. —Randy Myers

2026-the-disciple.title: The Disciple
2026-the-disciple.summary: Only one copy exists of hip hop royalty Wu-Tang Clan’s 2015 album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin —and that sold for $2 million at auction to an anonymous buyer later revealed to be fraudster Martin Shkreli. How that came to be is only one element of Joanna Natasegara’s captivating documentary that is essentially two films in one: the story of that notorious CD and of the man who conceptualized the idea that an album could be treated as the rarest of fine art. The first half of the film relates how Dutch-Moroccan rapper/producer Tarik “Cilvaringz” Azzougarh—a longtime Wu-Tang Clan fan—found his way into their inner circle, while the second delves into how Once Upon a Time in Shaolin and its unique circumstances came to be. Wu-Tang Clan leader RZA executive produced this wildly entertaining film that benefits from having an irrepressible narrator in Cilvaringz, who treats his own life as the stuff of legend, and the collision of art and commerce that the Shaolin affair came to represent.

2026-the-doctor-and-the-floating-bridge.title: The Doctor and the Floating Bridge
2026-the-doctor-and-the-floating-bridge.summary: A Korean expatriate doctor must confront his mixed feelings about his former home when he meets a very special patient.

2026-the-doll.title: The Doll
2026-the-doll.summary: Neglected by the boy who made her, a stitched doll injures herself again and again for his attention until the thread runs out and she's discarded.

2026-the-high-king-s-daughter.title: The High King's Daughter
2026-the-high-king-s-daughter.summary: In Joël Gibbs’s animated lush period romance, social class evokes something tender and mythic.

2026-the-illusion-of-an-everlasting-summ.title: The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer
2026-the-illusion-of-an-everlasting-summ.summary: Filmed over 25 years, this intimate documentary casts a tender and fearless eye over the lives of two inseparable cousins, Guillermina and Belinda, as they grow up in the rural Argentine Pampas. Celebrated photographer Alessandra Sanguinetti, in her prize-winning directorial debut, crafts a time capsule as fluid and heartrending as Boyhood and Seven Up! From carefree days playing dress-up and imagining vast futures, the girls mature before our eyes, dancing like no one is watching and ripening under the sun. In a blink, they tip into adulthood, effervescence fading under the weight of responsibility and narrowing options. Like a magic trick, though, their own daughters spring up to reclaim the joy of childhood as the camera keeps rolling. The heart of the narrative is the passage of time, but the film’s real power is how indelibly it captures women’s quiet resilience and the universal language of female friendship. Winner of the Filmmakers of the Present - Golden Leopard Award at the 2026 Locarno International Film Festival. —D. Quinones

2026-the-last-place-on-earth.title: The Last Place on Earth
2026-the-last-place-on-earth.summary: Play Trailer Deep in the breathtaking rainforests of Indonesia, an existential battle rages, to save Earth’s third-largest tropical rainforest from massive destruction caused by the palm oil boom, and with it, the future of the planet. This visually stunning, emotionally unsettling documentary captures the passion and purpose of Native people battling multinational corporations to save their homeland. Disturbing scenes reveal how illegal logging for the world’s most sought-after vegetable oil takes a devastating toll on lives and our planet’s climate. Filmed over nine years with a mostly Indonesian crew, David Booth Gardner captures activists overwhelmed by the race to save their lush jungles and endangered tigers, rhinos, elephants, and orangutans from smuggling, poaching, and the displacement of villagers, all under the watch of hovering drones. Inspiring and unnerving, this doc opens our eyes to these faraway battles, encouraging us all to lean in, speak up, and get involved in fighting corporate depredation for our global consumption. Executive produced by Louie Psihoyos ( The Cove ) and produced by the Oceanic Preservation Society. —Brendan Peterson

2026-the-liberation.title: The Liberation
2026-the-liberation.summary: Part slow-burn psychological thriller, part heart-wrenching family drama, The Liberation is filmmaker Guy Nattiv’s fictionalized portrayal of his grandmother’s life in the 1980s, and a visually lush deconstruction of the horrors of generational pain. Carrie Coon is at the top of her craft as Rita, a woman unravelling against the stress of her dead-end job, ever-demanding family, and the long-buried trauma she carries as a Holocaust survivor. When a chance encounter brings the free-spirited, charismatic Ricki (Lily James) into her orbit, Rita tastes the kind of freedom that life never afforded her through the all-female cult she steadily becomes a part of, cutting ties with her family as a result. While Rita’s teenage daughters (Bella Ramsey and Odessa Young) and her husband (Tracy Letts) see through the sinister undercurrents of Ricki’s tenets, they are woefully unprepared for the impossible task of rescuing a prisoner who doesn't want to be free. —Sofia Felino

2026-the-life-and-deaths-of-wilson-shedd.title: The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd
2026-the-life-and-deaths-of-wilson-shedd.summary: A relationship begins that pushes a couple down a rabbit hole of need, survival, promised freedom, and unexpected tragedy in writer/director Tim Blake Nelson’s powerful prison drama. Karen (Amanda Seyfried) volunteers as a creative writing teacher at the local penitentiary, a small window of escape from her abusive, unemployed, drunkard husband. Through reading the personal stories of the inmates, she forges an unexpected connection with one of them, Wilson Shedd (Scoot McNairy). Neither Karen nor Wilson are what they appear to be, and through Southern Gothic, nonlinear storytelling, the film peels the onions of their characters and hidden torments. Nelson (who also appears as the prison’s warden) does not just deliver a tale of two haunted souls but also provides a steely eyed, unblinkered gaze on capital punishment. The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd is a potent film that address real-world issues with compassion, poignancy, and vividness. —Sterling Hedgpeth

2026-the-man-i-love.title: The Man I Love
2026-the-man-i-love.summary: Play Trailer In late 1980s New York, Jimmy (Rami Malek), a theater artist living with AIDS, throws himself back into his work, rehearsing a new stage production while surrounded by lovers, family, friends, and fellow artists. Ira Sachs brings us into a world where fear and extraordinary creative energy exist side by side, capturing a generation determined to keep making art, falling in love, having sex, laughing, and living. Rather than turning the AIDS crisis into a conventional illness story, Sachs finds its presence in the relationships, silences, bodies, and choices of the people who lived through it. Malek gives Jimmy a magnetic, mercurial presence, while Tom Sturridge, Rebecca Hall, and Luther Ford bring intimacy, affection, and shifting loyalties into his world. Music becomes another language, with performances revealing what Jimmy cannot always say. Following Peter Hujar’s Day (MVFF48), Sachs returns to New York with a deeply sensual portrait of art, desire, community, and survival. —João Federici

2026-el-deshielo.title: El Deshielo
2026-el-deshielo.summary: Play Trailer The year is 1992, and the backdrop is Chile’s transition from Pinochet to democracy. In her long-awaited sophomore feature, director Manuela Martelli ( Chile ‘76 , MVFF45) returns to the country's disappeared, spinning out a political allegory through the perspective of nine-year-old Inés (Maya O’ Rourke), the story consistently framed at her eye level. A ski resort owned by Ines’s grandmother gleams against the frozen Andes. In grainy footage, an iceberg traverses the Atlantic Ocean and the screen, bound to a grandiose yet reluctant promise to remain unmelted. With an icy formal elegance, Martelli turns the shrill scrape of skis against snow into an eerie accomplice to Inés, after a guest's disappearance forces the child into the adults’ pact of silence. This Cannes premiere is unnerving, like the immaculate white landscape that surrounds it—a world beginning to thaw but still holding much of the iceberg that lies beneath its surface. —Ivonne Cotorruelo

2026-the-only-living-pickpocket-in-new-y.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
2026-the-only-living-pickpocket-in-new-y.summary: Play Trailer It’s hard out there for an aging pickpocket like Harry (a flawless John Turturro in an instantly iconic coat), an analog man facing a digital world where people no longer carry cash. Gracing the streets of New York with his traditional elegance, Harry finds a kindred spirit in his partner-in-crime Ben (Steve Buscemi), and lovingly cares for his nonverbal wife, before he accidentally antagonizes the wrong sort: the spoiled scion (Will Price) of a crime family. In sending Harry on a five-borough odyssey to salvage the situation, Noah Segan’s elegiac knockout gently mourns the adrift qualities of a bygone era, while romantically portraying the city’s diverse communities that our desperate, GPS-less protagonist relies on for acts of kindness. There is poetry in Segan’s mournfully textured lens, accompanied by jazzy beats and timeless Big Apple ballads. A love letter to one of cinema’s favorite towns, Segan’s unassuming character study joins the ranks of great NYC movies. —Tomris Laffly

2026-the-right-fit.title: The Right Fit
2026-the-right-fit.summary: In The Right Fit , Max Mollring and Nicolas Collins introduce the owner of a one-of-a-kind small business in San Rafael.

2026-the-shoe-thief.title: The Shoe Thief
2026-the-shoe-thief.summary: A mother and daughter discover something unexpected about themselves over a mysterious pair of shoes.

2026-the-spanish-lesson.title: The Spanish Lesson
2026-the-spanish-lesson.summary: In Simone Stadler’s The Spanish Lesson , a surprise student has some deeper resonance.

2026-the-unrooted-bloom.title: The Unrooted Bloom
2026-the-unrooted-bloom.summary: Alongside co-director Cassidy Friedman (Voices Beyond the Wall, Circles), visionary Bay Area poet, educator, and community activist Amber Allen-Peirson turns the camera on her own life in this deeply moving quest for belonging. A biracial woman living in Marin County, Allen-Peirson grapples with the complexities of her identity—of the nuances of living as a person with both Black and white roots in a nation founded on division. Using poetry to narrate a striking collage of archival footage and vérité moments from her present, Allen-Peirson deftly captures the ways in which she’s pulled in an overwhelming number of directions in her personal and professional lives. Torn between carrying on a legacy of fighting for what she believes in and simply trying to exist in an ever-demanding world, Allen-Peirson demonstrates that belonging can bloom through a life examined—in the pursuit of clarity. —Kate Bove

2026-the-white-elephant.title: The White Elephant
2026-the-white-elephant.summary: Inspired by the life of Queen Hsin Phyu Ma Shin and the late 19th-century massacre at Mandalay Palace—a tale of intrigue among the royalty in Myanmar.

2026-these-are-totally-real-animals.title: These Are Totally Real Animals
2026-these-are-totally-real-animals.summary: People imagine the animals we wish we could see in real life—all shapes, all colors!

2026-this-bright-light.title: This Bright Light
2026-this-bright-light.summary: Play Trailer Tamarin Luchessa seemed destined to burn brightly. An Olympic-bound rhythmic gymnast, her course was derailed by a diabetes diagnosis as a teenager. Her life became marked by medical crises, personal struggles, and eventually a kidney and pancreas transplant that altered her personality in ways even her family and friends could not recognize—only for her original self to return when the organs later began to fail. Sonoma County filmmaker Alexandra Lexton ( Fools’ Paradise (lost?) , MVFF47; The Lure of This Land , MVFF42) follows Tamarin’s mother, Cindy, from the mysteries of cellular memory into more ethereal terrain, where mediums, intuitives, and signs from beyond suggest our connections may extend past the physical body. Moving between science and spirit, this deeply personal docudrama chronicles a mother-daughter pact to help others, offering a loving reflection on life and death. —Michelle Svenson

2026-this-is-not-an-emergency.title: This is Not an Emergency
2026-this-is-not-an-emergency.summary: Two teenaged slackers do tarot readings in graveyards for cash ‘til their tagalong, screen-addicted baby brother takes off on his own.

2026-three-billboards-outside-ebbing-mis.title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
2026-three-billboards-outside-ebbing-mis.summary: Play Trailer While Three Billboards Outside Ebbing Missouri’s Mildred Hayes may go down as cinema history’s ultimate anti-heroine, Officer Dixon deserves kudos as her outclassed nemesis-turned-ally. In the film’s memorable ensemble, Mildred is played with unbridled cynicism and priceless, profane sarcasm by the inimitable Frances McDormand. She’s an inconsolable grieving mother with a triple-billboard-sized grudge and a fathomless rage demanding to be reckoned with. The ones doing the reckoning are the local police force: the beloved but ineffective Chief Willoughby (Woody Harrelson) and his hotheaded junior officer Dixon, a dimwitted, heavy-drinking momma's boy with a penchant for brutality, notably played by Sam Rockwell (MVFF49 Tributee and Oscar® winner for this performance)—with both hilarious and incendiary consequences. British playwright-turned-film-maker Martin McDonagh ( Seven Psychopaths , MVFF35; Wild Horse Nine , MVFF49 Opening Night) brings his singular brand of violence and black humor to this renegade masterpiece that surprises at every turn. But one thing remains constant: Hell definitely hath no fury like a Mildred Hayes ignored. Just ask Officer Dixon. —Joanne Parsont

2026-threeasfour-full-circle.title: threeASFOUR: FULL CIRCLE

guests.role: Dean, Cilker School of Art & Design (Moderator)

2026-threeasfour-full-circle.summary: From Björk to Chloë Sevigny to Meredith Monk, the New York City-based fashion collective threeASFOUR has dressed some of the world’s most avant-garde fashionistas in singular looks that blend nature and technology. While some write off runway couture as frivolous or banal, the visionary minds at threeASFOUR know that the human body is an endlessly fascinating art medium—something they prove time and again with their prescient designs. But as s the film points out, there are “certain things that get attention, [and] certain things that sell,” and for a fashion collective that favors vision and collaboration over all else that can prove challenging, especially in a multibillion-dollar industry that demands profit and favors easy, trend-making replication. Directed by Sean Ono Lennon and co-directed by Brian Gonzalez, this behind-the-scenes doc follows threeASFOUR co-founders Gabi Asfour, Angela Donhauser, and Adi Gil over several years as they pursue creative freedom and work that inspires unity. —Kate Bove

2026-to-be-loved.title: To Be Loved
2026-to-be-loved.summary: “My child, in this lifetime, you will know what it is to be loved.” A beautiful musical story of young love on the shores of a faraway land.

2026-together-apart.title: Together Apart
2026-together-apart.summary: A child of divorce learns how to appreciate time with Mom and time with Dad in a family that is together but apart.

2026-tete-a-tete.title: Tête à Tête
2026-tete-a-tete.summary: A trance-like dance of human and abstract forms. Undulating and shapeshifting to an irresistible rhythmic beat.

2026-union-town.title: Union Town
2026-union-town.summary: Two-time Best Documentary Feature Oscar® winner Barbara Kopple nabbed her first in 1976 for Harlan County, USA , which chronicled Kentucky coal miners’ bitter but ultimately successful strike for better working conditions. 1990’s American Dream was less upbeat: Threatened with pay cuts or no jobs at all, Minnesota meatpacking-plant workers found a decade of Reaganomics had thoroughly weakened their bargaining power. Decades later, the director’s focus is a whole new labor sector as she completes the trilogy she began 50 years ago. Those who serve UPS, Amazon, and apps like Door Dash deliver 2.4 million packages every day within NYC alone. Many aren’t official employees but third-party contractors sans benefits or job protection, their toil frequently underpaid, exhausting, sometimes downright dangerous. Meanwhile, the corporations themselves make astronomical profits. Can unions, activism, and strikes still secure livable wages, among other basics that are rapidly disappearing for many in the 21st century? Full of real-life drama and compelling personalities, Kopple’s latest is a true sign of our times. —Dennis Harvey

2026-until-we-meet-again.title: Until We Meet Again
2026-until-we-meet-again.summary: When the agents from the underworld come to her door, an elderly woman resists their call until certain conditions are met.

2026-we-are-the-land.title: We Are the Land
2026-we-are-the-land.summary: Coast Miwok and Southern Pomo stewards cultivate 7.6 acres of ancestral land at Heron's Shadow, sharing traditional practices and their harvest with the greater Bay Area.

2026-when-a-witness-recants.title: When a Witness Recants
2026-when-a-witness-recants.summary: With her trademark command of complex social issues and deeply human storytelling, veteran documentarian Dawn Porter (John Lewis: Good Trouble ) examines the Harlem Park Three—teenagers wrongfully sentenced to life in prison for the 1983 murder of a Baltimore middle schooler. Inspired by Jennifer Gonnerman’s New Yorker reporting, the investigative documentary tracks how police coerced 13 and 14-year-old witnesses into fabricating testimony, and how the state's case collapsed 36 years later in 2019, when those same witnesses formally recanted. Interweaving archival footage, graphic novel-style animation, and tense legal depositions, the film moves past the courtroom to capture the profound emotional toll on the trio, boys who became men behind bars, separated from their families and the world outside. Exploring the possibility of reconciliation between the exonerated and a key childhood witness, Porter ultimately asks what justice, accountability, and healing can look like in the wake of America's longest combined wrongful conviction. —Michelle Svenson

2026-when-you-give-a-cat-a-lemon.title: When You Give a Cat a Lemon
2026-when-you-give-a-cat-a-lemon.summary: A culinary whiz in the kitchen, this cat is a most unexpected cake-maker.

2026-where-the-silence-is-heard.title: Where the Silence is Heard
2026-where-the-silence-is-heard.summary: Play Trailer Gabriela Pena and Picho García’s deeply personal documentary delves into what isn’t expressed—the silences, unspoken fears, and absences that shape both Pena’s family history and her relationship with her mother. At the film’s outset, Pena moves to Valparaíso, the Chilean port city her family was forced from decades earlier amid the Pinochet regime. While reconnecting with her grandparents, the filmmaker takes on the formidable project of renovating the now-dilapidated house her family left behind. As she strips the former home to its core, Pena also digs into her relationship with her mother and how the physical distance between them could actually be a means of getting closer. Beautifully lensed and rivered by personal memories and archival footage, this achingly intimate family portrait explores how intergenerational trauma shapes how we love, all as one woman attempts to find peace before a new generation joins the story. —Kate Bove

2026-wicker.title: Wicker
2026-wicker.summary: Play Trailer Playing to the peak of their immaculate powers, Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, and Peter Dinklage bring grand charm, delight, and whimsy to this altogether unique and fantastical folk romance for the ages. Mocked by the eccentric, coupled townsfolk for her spinsterish manner, a fisherwoman (Colman) in this medieval world that is both wonderful and strange beseeches the local basket maker (Dinklage) to weave her a husband. He does, bringing to life the wicker man (Skarsgård) of her dreams, creating a cascading sensation throughout the village. Lushly designed, carefully crafted, and skillfully paced, this adaptation of Ursula Willis’s beguiling short story generated its own percolating buzz when it premiered at Sundance. Husband-and-wife directing duo Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson imbue their fractured tale with the liveliness and wit of master storytellers, weaving their mythical yarn with precision and captivating magic that is all too rare. —Landon Zakheim

2026-wild-east.title: Wild East
2026-wild-east.summary: Environmental activist Gabi Paun risks his life to expose illegal logging in Romania’s ancient forests, taking on timber mafias and IKEA while revealing the hidden cost of the world’s appetite for cheap furniture.

2026-windward.title: Windward
2026-windward.summary: Blind sailor Walt Raineri thought he'd prepared for his loss of sight but learns anew through sailing, navigating by listening, feeling, and trusting the wind, water, and his community.

2026-your-mother-your-mother-your-mother.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
2026-your-mother-your-mother-your-mother.summary: Play Trailer Academy Award® winner Mahershala Ali's turn as a devout Muslim who quietly makes his living as a professional killer headlines this elevated blend of exemplary action, taut thriller and moving drama resulting in a stunning work. In writer-director Bassam Tariq’s stirring fable, Ali’s Latif returns from his latest murder to a family in crisis and grief. Mourning the loss of his wife, Latif is left to care for his three children, including a newborn in desperate need of breast milk, while facing judgment from his community, pressure from a dangerous colleague, and the wrath of a potential new target, a fundamentalist gun-toting Christian zealot played by a sublime John Cho. Bolstered by a muscular directorial vision and impactful performances, Tariq’s emotional tale of vengeance, honor, and family offers incredible sweep and stunning skill that will linger in the bones and the soul. —Landon Zakheim
